summary: Identify the law of the integrand under the factorisation of θ^F_b (E), deduce integrability from the finite majorant (K), and compute the integral.

    any_goals fun_prop
    simp_all [weylElem_mul_left_comm, k.upperPairing_invariant, ψ, ↓frameGram_diag_mul]⟩
steps.claim: E: (z, c) ↦ ψ̃(v(c))·formIntegrandOne(b+1, W, z₁, weylRatio(b, p, q), w_b(p)v(c), z₂) under (𝖬^F × ((ζ ∗ θ^F_b) ∗ 𝗆^F_b)) × ρ(c)dc has the same law as (((x, g), σ), τ) ↦ ψ̃(στ⁻¹)·formIntegrandOne(b+1, W, x, weylRatio(b, p, q), σw_b(p)τ⁻¹, σg) under ((𝖬^F × 𝗆^F_b) × θ^F_b) × θ^F_b.

⟨by fun_prop [formIntegrandOne], by fun_prop [formIntegrandOne], ext_of_lintegral _ fun φ _ ↦ by
    simp (disch := with_unfolding_all fun_prop) [lintegral_map]
steps.claim: Both maps are measurable; compare the integrals of every test function.
Reduce to the inner integrals, for σ ∈ H_b.

steps.lean:
rw [← lintegral_floorMeasure_mul_right le_rfl
      (fun s _ ↦ by simp [-mul_assoc, mul_assoc s, k'.upperPairing_invariant, ← mul_assoc σ, ψ,
      ↓frameGram_diag_mul, *]) ⟨mem_unitriGroup_of_mem_floorGroup hσ, hσ⟩, hc, lintegral_mconv_symm,
      lintegral_congr_of_ae_imp z fun _ ↦ ?_] <;> try rw [lintegral_map]
steps.claim: Use the right invariance of θ^F_b under Q_{b+1} ∩ H_b (lintegral_floorMeasure_mul_right; the integrand is invariant by upperPairing_invariant and frameGram_diag_mul), the factorisation hc and Fubini; ζ is carried by Q_{b+1} ∩ H_b (z).
The integrands agree (w_b(p) commutes with H_b, the kernel is invariant, the diagonal frame entry is unchanged).

steps.lean:
have K : Integrable _ _ := ⟨E.2.aestronglyMeasurable, hm.lt_top.trans_le' (by
    grw [(enorm_mul ..).le, (ofReal_norm _).ge, (P.norm_psi _).le]
    simp (disch := with_unfolding_all fun_prop) [formMajorant, pivotModulus, lintegral_mul_const])⟩
steps.claim: K: the second function is integrable: |ψ̃| = 1 and the integral of the modulus is that of formMajorant, finite by hm.
J_T: so the first function is integrable too (E).

    ((((integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul' mρ hρ).1 J.integral_prod_right).const_mul
    _).const_mul t) (Or.inl (Or.inl E.integral_eq))
steps.claim: Hence Ψ (a.e. the c-section of the first function times t) is integrable, and by E and Fubini its integral is t·κ_b(p, q)·∫ (the second function) = t·floorForm(b, p, q, W, ψ̃).
